issues.problem:
Truly hidden round filler that reaches another part is kept and moves a tier. The SPEC's numbers for this case are stale and too small.

Why it happens: rule A only fires when a round part lies wholly inside ONE round hider, and the hull rule only when a facet's whole hull lies inside one. A rod or Ball that sits in a round pommel's band and runs on into the grip satisfies neither, so its band pieces read as showing.

issues.problem:
For a Wedge, the rank keys h1, h2, h3 are its half extents as given, and they are compared before the material's name. §4.4 says the order is "a Block's sorted half extents, the name of the material, then half extents as given".

So for two coincident writings of one Wedge in one slot, the writing decides which material is kept. For a Block, the material's name decides.

Repro, wedge_mat.luau: F4 plus its tip written as (sx, sz, sy) with the half turn, in the Blade.
- Tip Iron, other writing Steel: the Iron tip is kept, governing material Iron, mass 3.230320.
- Tip Steel, other writing Iron: the Steel tip is kept, so S3's m_material is Steel and T is 1.02, mass 3.229776.
- The Block's two writings keep the Iron one both ways (mass 3.230320).
No tier moves, since difficultyTerm is 0 for both materials.

issues.problem:
§4.4 calls rule A exact for a Cylinder in a Ball (Shapes.maxDist). But maxDist takes perp = sqrt(max(0, dd - a·a)). On or near the rod's axis line through the Ball's centre, that leaves the square root of rounding, about 1e-9 too high (maxdist_err.luau: up to 9.35e-10 for rods 0.1-5.9 long).

Repro (out\x4_11.txt design 708, dbg708.luau): a rod coaxial with a higher-ranked Ball, its rim 9.9855e-8 out of it. That is within EPS_GEOM, so it should show nothing. Cover computes 1.0030e-7 and reads 9.2 % of the rod.

On 2,500 tangles (seed 11) with my brute force's tie set to 1e-12, there are 52 facets outside the bracket in 3 designs, worst 10.7 % of a part. All are this case.

It is a tie band about 1e-9 wide at EPS_GEOM. No plausible design is affected.
issues.fix:
Tried in scratchpad m2x-v1-4\fixD (diff out\fixD_cover.diff). Replace the line `return Shapes.maxDist(P, Q.cx, Q.cy, Q.cz) - Q.r` with:

`local best = 0`
`for s = -1, 1, 2 do`
`  local dx, dy, dz = P.cx + s * P.hx * P.ux - Q.cx, P.cy + s * P.hx * P.uy - Q.cy, P.cz + s * P.hx * P.uz - Q.cz`
`  local a = dx * P.ux + dy * P.uy + dz * P.uz`
`  local px, py, pz = dx - a * P.ux, dy - a * P.uy, dz - a * P.uz`
`  local perp = sqrt(px * px + py * py + pz * pz) + P.r`
`  best = max(best, a * a + perp * perp)`
`end`
`return sqrt(best) - Q.r`

summary:
M2 after fix round 3 does not pass: 2 major and 3 minor issues stand. I edited only copies under my scratch folder, and committed nothing.

Round 3's own fixes hold:
- The band filler that was last round's blocker is now cleaned.
- Rule A and the hull rule agree with my independent brute force: 0 errors outside the bracket on about 41,000 parts in round-heavy tangles, and no NaN or inf.
- Against round 3's base, only units move on the plausible set, the attack corpus and the fixtures, matching the fixer's counts exactly.
- Results are bit-identical under random orders, copies placed first or last, Dust, and other writings of a Block or Wedge. Mirror images differ only in the class §17.2 allows.
- The Wedge rank tie is fixed, the 4 % precision bound holds on a new seed, and the cap, reports, raised checkpoints and timing match §4.9.

Major 1: truly hidden round filler that reaches another part is kept and moves a tier.
- Repro: F5 with a Ball pommel 0.6 across and its blade 0.25 longer, plus 4 Blade rods in the crease where the grip enters the pommel.
- Every point of each rod is at least 0.002 inside the pommel or the grip, and the truth reads 0.000 % on 400,000 points.
- The build reads 6.57 % each and keeps them, so Sharpening goes from 0.1827 Normal to 0.2083 Hard.
- §17.2 and E-S2.12 still say this case reads at most 2.04 % with no tier. That figure came from V1's trial tree, which had no rule A, and on the build that family reads 0.
- I tried a code option in a copy (a hull test on the polygons left after all hiders). It closes the rods with 0 plausible verdicts moved and +0.16 % units, but it is partial and needs CoverBrute support. The decision is the lead's; the SPEC text has to change either way.

Major 2: rule (i)'s price is understated. The moved-out half-spaces stand up to 0.0452 r past a Ball's true surface, not 0.026 r, so visible parts are cleaned:
- a Block truly 17.3 % visible on a Ball pommel;
- a plate truly 18.1 % visible on a round guard;
- 4 visible studs in a sword, which flips Sharpening from 0.2047 Hard (the truth's row) to 0.1907 Normal.

Minors:
- A Wedge's as-given extents decide its rank before the material, so the writing of a coincident copy picks the surviving material and the mass. Fix tried.
- Rule A's Cylinder-in-Ball value is about 1e-9 off on a rod's axis line. Fix tried: the strict-tie misses go from 52 to 0.
- Eleven behaviour-changing mutants of rule A survive the suite, and CoverBrute misreads a part on a rod's axis line. A new Cover.spec case plus a one-line CoverBrute fix kills all eleven; verify is green with them, 597 pass and 0 fail.
